newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar eases, extra quota release expected.
newsitem.headline: India sugar eases, extra quota release expected.

text.p: Indian sugar prices lost some of their recent gains as expectations the government may release a higher quota for the coming months sparked profit-taking, traders said.
Fresh consumer demand and enquiries from the retailers also pittered out, they said.
Generally in the summer months government releases higher free sale quota of sugar as demand in these months is generally higher.
"Free sale quota of sugar for the current month is 700,000 tonnes and traders were expecting that government may announce quota of 750,000 tonnes for April," one broker said.
"Quota for May may be announced higher at 800,000 tonnes and for June it may announce at 825,000 tonnes," he said.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 8/13 rupees to 1,265/1,305 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved down by 15 rupees at 1,305/1,375 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery fell by 5/10 rupees at 1,210/1,225 rupees per quintal.
